title: Introduce modular gpu nodepool attach/detach modules and tfstate epoch isolator
author: Priya Nair
description:
Motivation: Private deployments have accumulated a large, brittle monolithic tfstate for GPU nodepools, IAM bindings and subnet attachments. That layout makes targeted upgrades and tenant-scoped rollbacks expensive and error-prone. This change introduces two complementary patterns: (1) modular attach/detach TF modules for nodepool-to-subnet and nodepool-iam lifecycle (idempotent attachments), and (2) a tfstate 'epoch isolator' that splits state into epoch-scoped slices to enable safe in-place migrations and partial rollbacks.

Summary of changes: modularized nodepool attachment primitives and introduced an epoch-based tfstate isolator + a small CLI to coordinate migrations. Includes migration plan, tests, and a rollback workflow. The PR is intentionally conservative: no automatic destructive renames, idempotent operations only, and a canary migration mode.

What is included (high level):
- A new module modules/nodepool-attachment that encapsulates: subnet claim, cross-account route attachment, and IAM role binding for nodepools (attach/detach lifecycle with explicit detach timeout).
- A new module modules/tfstate-epoch-isolator that exposes a namespaced backend key pattern and helper resources to create an "epoch" anchor and migration lock.
- A lightweight CLI tools/tfstate-epoch that implements: prepare-epoch, snapshot-checksum, migrate-epoch --canary, rollback-epoch. The CLI uses the existing terraform state mv + state pull/push under a lock to create deterministic epoch artifacts.
- Migration docs and a step-by-step canary plan in docs/migrations/tfstate-epoch.md.
- Unit tests for the modules (module tests with local backend mocks) and an integration harness that runs a full canary migration in CI using a disposable GCS backend.

Migration plan (recommended):
1) Run tools/tfstate-epoch prepare-epoch --tenant <T> --epoch 0001 to create epoch anchor (no state move).
2) Verify checksums: tools/tfstate-epoch snapshot-checksum --epoch 0001 --tenant <T>.
3) Run tools/tfstate-epoch migrate-epoch --tenant <T> --epoch 0001 --canary. This will copy nodepool-related resources into a new epoch-prefixed key and update the nodepool-attachment module references (via a small pointer map).
4) Smoke test low-traffic tenant workloads for 24h. If green, run migrate without --canary to finalize.

Rollback notes: The epoch isolator keeps an immutable snapshot for each epoch. Rollback is a two-step: tools/tfstate-epoch rollback-epoch --tenant <T> --epoch 0001 will re-establish previous pointer maps and reattach nodepools to the old state. Because we avoid destructive renames, rollback is expected to be fast and safe. The docs include emergency steps to reattach nodes if the cloud provider shows delayed detach.

Compatibility and safety:
- Existing workflows continue to operate against legacy backend key until migration is finalized.
- Nodepool-attachment module exposes a detach_grace_period and attach_precheck flags to avoid racey detach+recreate during migration.
- IAM credentials rotation and HSM/KMS integration unchanged; module only wires existing role templates.

Testing and CI:
- Added a CI job "tfstate-epoch:migration-canary" that runs the full canary on a temporary GCS bucket and applies the canary migration using service account creds in CI. The job is gated behind a manual trigger to avoid flakiness.
- Unit and integration tests added under test/modules and test/integration/tfstate-epoch.

Checklist:
- [x] Module: nodepool-attachment implemented and documented
- [x] Module: tfstate-epoch-isolator implemented and documented
- [x] CLI: tools/tfstate-epoch with prepare/migrate/rollback/checksum commands
- [x] Canary migration doc and runbook
- [x] CI: canary job and unit/integration tests

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: provider-specific behavior on state mv (some clouds rate-limit state ops). Mitigation: CLI retries and exponential backoff; recommend off-hours canary windows.
- Risk: ephemeral detaches cause scheduling churn. Mitigation: detach_grace_period default 10m and attach_precheck prevents immediate reattach churn.

Related work: This complements ENG-7423 (gpu pool lifecycle operator) and SUP-2091 where customers saw large tfstate apply times during upgrades. The epoch pattern is intentionally generic and can be reused for other large resource families (PVCs, DNS zones).

review_thread: Ethan Cole: Please add a canary plan in docs and ensure the CLI is idempotent. Also request you document expected timing for a migration on a 200-tenant install.
Priya Nair: Addressed in docs/migrations/tfstate-epoch.md; added timing estimates and an idempotent prepare step. Updated CLI to double-check the lock and perform checksum-then-copy pattern.

Diego Ramos: Found a race in attach_precheck when multiple nodes re-register quickly. Suggest introducing a short backoff and prometheus metric. Update: added prometheus metric nodepool_attachment_retries_total and backoff in CLI.
Lena Park: Reviewed IAM templating and requested explicit role name prefix to avoid cross-tenant collisions. PR updated to include tenant-scoped role prefix.
Ethan Cole: CI job is manual which is good. Approve after addressing minor doc nits.

release_notes:
Introduce nodepool-attachment TF module and tfstate-epoch-isolator to enable safer, epoch-scoped tfstate migrations for GPU nodepools. Adds a CLI to perform canary migrations, plus a documented rollback path.
Impact: migration is opt-in and gated by the tfstate-epoch CLI. No immediate behavioral changes until migration is executed.
notes_for_ops: Recommended canary window: 2-4 hours during low-traffic; ensure Cloud provider rate limits are checked. Run the CLI with --dry-run first to verify checksums. Keep a copy of original backend snapshot outside the bucket for emergency restores.
